jobs.title: Environmental Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
We are looking for a talented  Environmental Strategy Manager  to join our  team  in  Environment  for Cummins  Daventry, Northamptonshire, United Kingdom.

In this role, you will make an impact in the following ways:

-
Lead regulatory sensing and analysis for assigned environmental and product non-emissions regulatory areas, interpreting complex technical, legal, and regulatory documents and translating requirements into clear guidance for the business.

-
Anticipate emerging regulatory developments, assess their technical, commercial, and strategic impacts, and provide actionable recommendations to leaders, technical experts, and product teams to manage risks and opportunities.

-
Develop and lead company regulatory positions and advocacy strategies, defining engagement objectives, timelines, key messages, external partners, and actions required to influence emerging environmental and product regulations.

-
Lead cross-functional regulatory advocacy programs from inception through completion, partnering with Engineering, Compliance, Product, Legal, Government Relations, and other stakeholders to align positions and deliver agreed regulatory outcomes.

-
Build and maintain effective relationships with regulators, industry associations, customers, and other external stakeholders, representing company interests and communicating constructively across global markets and diverse audiences.

-
Develop and communicate regulatory intelligence, strategic recommendations, educational materials, and unified regulatory messages to internal stakeholders, ensuring complex environmental and regulatory topics are clearly understood.

-
Develop strategic frameworks and analyses that synthesize environmental data, stakeholder input, regulatory trends, risks, and opportunities to support business strategy, product planning, compliance activities, and informed decision-making.

-
Manage multiple cross-functional regulatory projects and continuous improvement initiatives, including project scope, timelines, risks, resources, tools, and processes, while identifying process gaps, implementing improvement plans, and sharing lessons learned across teams.
Education/ Experience:
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Environmental Policy, Law, Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Business, or a related technical or scientific discipline; a Master’s or other advanced degree is preferred, with legal training or a legal background strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience in environmental and/or regulatory policy, with a strong understanding of emerging product regulatory requirements and their implications for business and product strategies.
- Proven experience leading global initiatives and cross-functional teams, working effectively across organizational boundaries and with internal and external stakeholders to deliver strategic regulatory outcomes.
- Experience engaging with EU policymakers, trade associations, and industry groups is strongly preferred; previous experience in government, a trade association, or strategic regulatory development is an advantage.
- Working knowledge of major EU materials and product regulatory frameworks, including EU POPs, REACH, RoHS, WEEE, ESPR, and the EU Battery Regulation, with experience partnering with in-house counsel to assess emerging product regulatory risks.
To be successful in this role you will need the following:

- Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional subject matter expert teams and projects, independently coordinating internal and external initiatives across organizational boundaries to achieve shared objectives.
- Strong environmental acumen, with knowledge of environmental topics and trends related to air, exhaust, water, waste, sustainability, and/or materials, and the ability to assess environmental data and business impacts.
- Strong strategic and analytical thinking skills, with the ability to interpret complex and sometimes contradictory information, conduct gap analyses, benchmark current and desired states, and develop actionable recommendations and strategies.
- Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build partnerships, communicate effectively across organizational boundaries, and establish trust through integrity, authenticity, and transparent engagement.
- Strong planning, project, and risk management skills, with the ability to prioritize work, manage project issues and risks, establish timelines, and deliver commitments aligned with organizational goals.
- Ability to develop and improve systems and processes, using structured approaches to eliminate inefficiencies, address roadblocks, document workflows, and implement sustainable solutions that improve organizational effectiveness.
Leads processes to determine discipline positions on strategic environmental and business priorities and leads and internal and external stakeholder engagement. Manages, develops, and implements programs composed of multiple cross functional projects. Partners with key business stakeholders to ensure a successful project completion. Manages the design, development and implementation of tools and processes which facilitates the achievement of functional excellence. Partners with discipline leadership to identify process gaps, and develops improvement plans. Coordinates and monitors the execution of the improvement projects for a given area.

jobs.title: Corporate Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced strategy professional to help shape the strategic direction of Cummins’ Distribution Business across Asia Pacific. This newly created regional role will work closely with senior leaders on some of the business’s most important growth, profitability and transformation priorities – from framing complex strategic questions through to recommendations and execution.

The role offers exposure across markets, businesses and senior leadership, with the flexibility to be based in any Australian capital city or Singapore.

In this role, you will make an impact in the following ways:

-
Lead high-impact strategic initiatives and workstreams across business units, growth opportunities and new ventures

-
Develop business strategies using qualitative and quantitative analysis to evaluate opportunities, challenges and potential solutions

-
Generate strategic insights from market, financial, environmental, stakeholder and business data to support decision-making

-
Partner with senior regional and global leaders and key stakeholders to influence strategic direction and outcomes

-
Lead cross-functional initiatives, resolving complex challenges and driving strategic priorities through to execution

-
Communicate complex strategic concepts and recommendations clearly through compelling written and verbal presentations

-
Lead through influence, providing strategic guidance on complex business challenges while coaching and building capability across project teams
Being part of Cummins means working alongside today’s most innovative thinkers to solve the world’s toughest problems. We are proud to offer learning and development opportunities designed to promote individual performance and spark purpose and trust within our teams. We look to hire the best and then help you to become even better.
To be successful in this role you will need the following:
•    Demonstrated experience solving complex strategic business problems and leading initiatives through to execution
•    Strong strategic thinking, structured problem-solving and analytical capability, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and test hypotheses
•    Strong execution focus, translating strategic analysis and recommendations into tangible business outcomes
•    Proven ability to influence, communicate and present effectively with VP and senior executive-level stakeholders
•    Experience working across countries, functions and diverse stakeholder groups within a complex organisation
•    Corporate strategy, strategy consulting or equivalent strategy-related experience highly regarded, ideally within a similar heavy industrial or B2B environment
•    Master’s degree in Business Administration or equivalent preferred

jobs.title: IAM Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Job Summary:
Responsible for leading the organization’s cybersecurity operations team, with a primary focus on incident response, threat monitoring, and the execution of cybersecurity strategies, policies, and risk management practices to safeguard the organization’s systems, data, and infrastructure. The manager serves as a coach and mentor to security professionals, builds operational processes aligned with best practices and industry standards, and partners with engineering, IT, and business to protect critical systems, infrastructure, and data from evolving threats. Serves as an accountable leader for the people, processes, and technologies that prevent, detect, investigate, and contain cyber threats across enterprise, cloud, and OT environments. Owns SecOps outcomes (24×7 monitoring & incident response), the detection engineering program (use-case lifecycle, signal quality, automation), and the threat hunting program

Key Responsibilities:
Leads the execution of complex responses to computer security incidents in alignment with organizational policies and industry best practices. Coordinates and communicates with multiple business units during incidents, providing updates and actionable recommendations. Oversees root cause analysis and ensures that lessons learned are integrated into improved processes and protections. Leads teams in assessing severity, developing mitigation strategies, and prioritizing risk reduction activities. Monitors security-related intelligence sources (e.g., SANS, BugTraq) to maintain situational awareness of current attacks and trends. Collaborates with Cybersecurity Engineering teams and business to communicate risks and recommend security enhancements. Ensures that security technologies employed by the operations and incident response teams support and enhance operational processes. Identifies opportunities to improve operational efficiency, standard operating procedures, and incident response playbooks. Leads the application of recognized cybersecurity and IT frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO, ITIL, COBIT) in alignment with organizational processes and controls. Manages, coaches, and mentors cybersecurity operations staff, fostering a culture of learning, accountability, and continuous improvement. Defines team objectives, evaluates performance, and supports professional growth through training and development. Participates in industry task forces and working groups to stay informed on evolving threats and best practices, and fosters a culture of continuous improvement in cybersecurity practices and awareness. Contributes to organizational situational awareness by managing and leveraging cybersecurity data sources.

This role will also be responsible for execution of IAM strategies, policies, and risk management practices to safeguard the organization’s systems, data, and infrastructure. Key duties include managing team workflows, enforcing service-level agreements, and running security tools like Saviynt, MS Entra, CyberArk etc.

jobs.title: Executive Director – Leadership Development & Enterprise Capability Building
jobs.description:
At Cummins, leadership capability is a strategic advantage that enables our people, teams, and business to thrive in an increasingly dynamic and complex environment. Executive Director – Leadership Development & Enterprise Capability Building has a unique opportunity to shape how leadership is developed and applied across the enterprise, from frontline leaders and emerging influencers to senior executives and officers. As the steward of Cummins' Leadership Development Architecture, you will establish the frameworks, experiences, and standards that build the leadership capabilities required to advance our Mission, Values & Promise along with our long-term business strategy.

Leading a global team of development experts, you will create an integrated leadership ecosystem that connects executive development, leadership capability building, coaching, and talent growth across all levels of the organization. You will partner closely with senior business leaders, HR stakeholders, external thought leaders, and executive leadership, including CEO Jen Rumsey, to strengthen Cummins' leadership bench, accelerate readiness for future challenges, and sustain Jen’s leadership legacy that will drive the company's continued success.

This highly visible leadership role requires strategic vision, enterprise influence, and deep expertise in leadership development. Success will be measured by your ability to build leadership capability at scale, foster inclusive and high-performing leadership cultures, and deliver measurable business impact through a world-class leadership development architecture.

Based in Indianapolis or Columbus, Indiana, this onsite-with-flexibility role is intentionally designed to enable meaningful face-to-face engagement, collaboration, and coaching with senior leaders and stakeholders across the enterprise. Relocation assistance is available.

- Define and lead Cummins’ enterprise leadership development strategy and Leadership Development Architecture (LDA), ensuring leadership capabilities enable business objectives, workforce evolution, and enterprise transformation.

- Build leadership capability across all employee and leader populations by creating connected development pathways, experiences, and tools that support growth throughout key career and leadership transitions.

- Lead the identification, prioritization, development, and measurement of critical leadership capabilities that strengthen organizational performance, succession readiness, and long-term business success.

- Direct the executive development portfolio, integrating coaching, assessments, sponsorship, mentoring, enterprise exposure, and experiential learning to accelerate senior leadership readiness and effectiveness.

- Establish enterprise standards, methodologies, quality expectations, and governance practices that elevate the consistency, effectiveness, and impact of leadership development globally.

- Partner across HR and business functions to ensure leadership development is integrated with talent management, organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, succession management, and employee experience strategies.

- Leverage external research, leadership trends, learning science, leadership analytics, and responsible AI-enabled solutions to drive innovation and continuously improve leadership outcomes.

- Build and lead a high-performing global team while fostering inclusive leadership practices, equitable access to development opportunities, measurable business impact, and a culture of continuous learning and growth.

jobs.description:
2439344 Payroll Tax/Compliance Manager

At Cummins, we believe your passion is your power. Supercharge your career with the support of a global team that empowers you to do your best work.

We are looking for a talented Payroll Tax/Compliance Manager  to join our Payroll team  for Cummins Services – HR Operations  at Cummins Comercializadora  in San Luis Potosí, SLP, Mexico.

Work Modality: Hybrid, 3 days on site, 2 days home office.

In this role, you will make an impact in the following ways:

- Serve as the primary payroll tax subject matter expert for multi-state U.S. and Canadian payroll operations, ensuring ongoing compliance with federal, state, local, and provincial tax regulations.

- Independently research, analyze, and resolve complex payroll tax issues, agency inquiries, and notices from the IRS, state and local tax authorities, CRA, and provincial agencies.

- Lead payroll tax compliance activities related to employee hires, transfers, and organizational changes, ensuring accurate tax withholding and reporting setup.

- Engage directly in communications with federal, state, local, and Canadian tax agencies to resolve escalated tax matters and compliance issues.

- Conduct detailed audits and reviews of employee tax configurations, payroll tax withholdings, and system setups to identify and mitigate compliance risks.

- Oversee payroll tax adjustments, amendments, and corrections, including complex W-2/W-2c processing and employee tax record remediation.

- Perform advanced analysis, reconciliations, and research to support payroll tax audits, regulatory examinations, and compliance initiatives.

- Review and validate quarterly and annual payroll tax filings, including Forms 941, 940, W-2, W-2c, T4, Quebec Releve 1 and QPP, EI, QPIP and WCB   and other required U.S. and Canadian tax reporting.

- Provide expertise in Canadian payroll tax compliance, including CPP, EI, EHT, federal and provincial tax requirements, and year-end reporting obligations.

- Review state unemployment insurance rate notices, assess impacts, and coordinate implementation with payroll vendors and internal stakeholders.

- Evaluate and oversee new tax account registrations, jurisdictional filing requirements, and agency account maintenance activities.

- Partner with payroll vendors, HR, Finance, and external agencies to resolve complex tax matters and ensure accurate payroll tax reporting and remittance.

- Support internal and external audits by providing technical guidance, documentation, and analysis related to payroll tax compliance.

- Identify opportunities to improve payroll tax processes, controls, and compliance procedures, driving operational efficiencies and risk reduction. Collaborate with technical teams to provide use cases and test configuration changes and new development for tax law changes.

To be successful in this role, you will need the following:
- 5-8 years of experience managing a team responsible for US, CA payroll tax. UR-PR is a plus.
- In-depth knowledge of federal, state, and local payroll tax laws and regulations, including IRS guidelines.
- Experience in a large, complex organization (e.g., 5000+ employees and multiple entities).
- Proven ability to lead/ supervise tax analysts for minimum 3 years
- Experience with ADP Global View or SAP and ADP Smart Compliance
- Excellent written and oral communication skills in both English and Spanish.
- Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment and collaborate with multiple stakeholders.
- Strong analytical and process diagnostic skills, capable of understanding both details and the bigger picture.

Preferred:
- French Canadian language level a plus.

Competencies:

- Strategic Tax Planning

- Tax Based Modeling and Computation

- Technical Tax Analysis

- Action oriented

- Being resilient

- Manages ambiguity

- Nimble learning

- Resourcefulness

- Project Management

- Values differences

- US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles

Education, Licenses, and Certifications:
Bachelor’s degree in accounting or administration.
Leads the Payroll Tax and Compliance function supporting U.S. and Canadian payroll operations. Responsible for managing and developing the payroll tax team, overseeing complex tax compliance activities, and ensuring adherence to federal, state, local, and provincial requirements. Serves as a key subject matter expert for payroll tax matters, including regulatory inquiries, audits, tax filings, employee tax configurations, and year-end reporting. Partners with HR, Finance, tax authorities, and technical teams to resolve complex issues, strengthen controls, mitigate compliance risks, and drive continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Marketing & Sales Leader - On-Highway
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

Effectively manages the relationship and business strategies for large, complex assigned accounts (cross-regional, global, etc.) to grow our share of the customer's wallet and achieve sales goals. Strengthens existing customer relationships and builds additional relationships within accounts.

Key Responsibilities:

Develops, manages, and expands business relationships with assigned accounts, for example by understanding and using their industry terminology and understanding their business model and buying process.

Identifies current and emerging customer needs. Develops and executes account strategies to grow share with existing accounts and supports new business opportunities.

Gains agreement to the benefits of Cummins products and solutions by helping customers make sense of available data and information.

Grows Cummins’ share of the customer’s business. Negotiates and implements contracts with accounts as authorized, for example by managing customer questions and managing escalations for accounts receivable and/or payment terms.

Achieves revenue and share goals associated with revenue and profit targets.

Models (and manages, for direct reports) use of the Cummins Sales Process. Provides timely and accurate reports and forecasts on the assigned schedule, using Cummins tools and processes and Customer Relationship Management systems.

Develops and executes account sales plans in support of business strategy. Develops growth or new business opportunities jointly with accounts and supports initiatives to increase customer value.

Mentors, motivates, and develops less experienced sales and/or account team staff.

NA

Customer focus - Building strong customer relationships and delivering customer-centric solutions.

Integrates Customer Perspective - Incorporates an understanding of the customers' perspective on our products and sales efforts to develop sales content that improves our ability to meet their needs and increase revenue.

jobs.title: Senior Business Development Specialist
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Human Resources Business Partner Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
We are looking for a talented Human Resources Business Partner Manager (m/w/d) to join our team in Alsdorf, Germany .

A Unique Role: Cummins HRBP Manager, embedded at NPROXX

This is a  Cummins role dedicated to  NPROXX, a 100% Cummins-owned business that operates with a high degree of independence and is not fully integrated into Cummins' processes, policies, and systems. This makes it a rare opportunity: you stay within Cummins — with the full support, resources, and career network of our HR function and Centers of Excellence behind you — while working inside a smaller, entrepreneurial company where you can build new skills, shape HR strategy, and take on responsibilities well beyond the typical Cummins HRBP scope.

NPROXX is a world leader in high pressure hydrogen storage for both stationary and mobile applications.

The role reports directly to the EBU HRBP Director (Mariana Gaviao).

In this role, you will make an impact in the following ways:

- Serve as the senior HR leader for NPROXX and a member of the Leadership Team/Management Board, providing strategic HR support and input at the highest level. Acting as the primary HR partner to NPROXX leadership, you will operate with broader, more end-to-end ownership than a typical Cummins HRBP — spanning strategic partnership through to hands-on HR generalist and operational topics.

- Lead and develop a team of two HR Generalists, one based in Alsdorf, Germany and one in Heerlen, The Netherlands — setting direction, building capability, and overseeing HR delivery across both locations.

- Provide expert HR support aligned with local regulations in both locations — Germany and The Netherlands — ensuring practices reflect country-specific employment law and the requirements of each legal entity.

- Own and manage Works Council and union engagement in Germany, partnering constructively on co-determination topics, consultations, and negotiations, and ensuring NPROXX maintains strong, compliant, and trust-based employee relations.

- Oversee NPROXX's established HR operations and identify opportunities for improvement. NPROXX already has its own HR policies and handbook, payroll, and benefits in place; the HR Generalists and the ADP payroll vendor run the day-to-day processes. In this role you will manage that delivery, assess where practices can be strengthened, and lead the resulting improvements.

- Identify and act on opportunities aligned to the HR strategy, proactively spotting where talent, organization, culture, and capability work can advance NPROXX's business goals — and leading those initiatives end-to-end.

- Leverage the Cummins HR ecosystem as a thought partner. NPROXX manages its own HR activities. This role can draw on Cummins' Centers of Excellence, Total Rewards, and broader HR community for ideas, tools, and select resources — collaborating on solutions that are tailored to NPROXX's specific needs rather than adopted off-the-shelf.

- Advise with impact: Partner with stakeholders to deliver balanced, practical HR solutions.
- Solve strategically: Tackle complex challenges with a structured, insight-driven approach.
- Willingness to work onsite in Germany and travel regularly to the Netherlands (approx. 35-minute drive).

jobs.title: GEOS ISO 17025 Strategy Leader

- Provide leadership in resolving complex, ambiguous system issues with potential global impact, ensuring robust, scalable solutions.

jobs.title: Sourcing Manager

Defines and evaluates a collaborative relationship with a category’s key/strategic suppliers to deliver value to Cummins and the supplier.

AI Lab Infrastructure & Operations Manager

Cummins AI Lab - Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
About Cummins AI Lab
The Cummins AI Lab integrates applied AI research, engineering workflows, manufacturing processes, and enterprise platforms to deliver high-value AI solutions across Cummins' global operations. We build and operate the infrastructure, technology ecosystem, and experimentation environment that enable rapid AI innovation, proof-of-concept validation, and scalable enterprise AI adoption.
Role Overview
The AI Lab Infrastructure & Operations Manager owns the reliable, secure, and efficient operation of the AI Lab environment. The role manages software platforms, AI services, hardware assets, computing resources, lab infrastructure, vendors, contractors, and supporting team members. It ensures that researchers, solution architects, and project teams can access fit-for-purpose platforms, tools, environments, and operational support.
This is a management and technical enablement role. The emphasis is on technology evaluation, introduction, governance, resource optimization, service continuity, and operational excellence rather than deep architecture design, platform engineering, or framework development.
Key Responsibilities
1. Software Platform & AI Service Operations
- Manage AI cloud environments, AI platforms, hosted AI services, model APIs, and related service subscriptions used by the AI Lab.

- Coordinate the onboarding, configuration, operation, maintenance, and lifecycle management of AI services and platforms.

- Evaluate and introduce external foundation models, model inference services, deployment frameworks, and technical tools based on lab needs.

- Conduct fit-for-purpose technical assessments covering usability, compatibility, reliability, security, operational effort, scalability, and cost.

- Maintain service inventories, ownership records, operating guidance, access models, and support processes for lab software capabilities.

- Coordinate incident resolution, service changes, renewals, and escalation with internal IT teams and external providers.

2. Hardware Infrastructure & Computing Resource Management
- Manage AI all-in-one servers, AI mobile workstations, GPU computing resources, lab devices, and related infrastructure assets.

- Plan and coordinate resource allocation, workload scheduling, capacity usage, and computing availability across AI Lab activities.

- Monitor utilization, availability, maintenance status, and operational risks, and recommend actions to improve effective resource use.

- Own hardware inventory, assignment, maintenance coordination, upgrade planning, warranty tracking, and lifecycle management.

- Coordinate equipment installation, configuration, technical support, and issue resolution with vendors, contractors, and enterprise IT teams.

3. AI Lab Environment, Network & Operational Governance
- Lead day-to-day management and operations of the AI Lab infrastructure environment.

- Coordinate lab environment readiness, network connectivity, access, accounts, permissions, storage, and supporting services.

- Establish and maintain operating standards for resource requests, environment access, equipment usage, change management, incident handling, and asset governance.

- Maintain operational documentation, service runbooks, inventories, usage records, and management dashboards.

- Drive service continuity, issue prevention, operational risk management, and continuous improvement for lab infrastructure and services.

4. Data Security, Compliance & Risk Coordination
- Coordinate data security, cybersecurity, privacy, and compliance requirements for AI Lab platforms, models, devices, networks, and external services.

- Partner with enterprise IT, cybersecurity, architecture, procurement, legal, and relevant governance teams to complete required reviews and controls.

- Support access control, data classification, secure configuration, logging, patching, vulnerability handling, and risk remediation processes.

- Assess operational and security implications before introducing external models, cloud services, inference frameworks, or new devices.

- Maintain risk, issue, exception, and remediation tracking for the lab infrastructure environment.

5. Technology Evaluation & Lab Enablement
- Scan and evaluate emerging AI infrastructure technologies, AI services, model deployment options, inference frameworks, hardware solutions, and productivity tools.

- Organize trials and technical evaluations with solution architects, research scientists, users, contractors, and vendors.

- Provide practical recommendations on platform selection, service adoption, resource use, operational readiness, and future infrastructure needs.

- Enable PoC teams by provisioning suitable environments, coordinating computing resources, and resolving infrastructure dependencies.

- Capture evaluation findings, limitations, operating requirements, and recommendations for reuse across the AI Lab.

6. Vendor, Contractor & Budget Management

- Demonstrated experience coordinating complex, high-stakes, and time-sensitive projects involving multiple internal stakeholders and external service providers.
